body:
Four prompt builders splice externally-authored text straight into an LLM prompt without routing it through @adlc/core's fence(). Found by the completeness sweep added in #1005/#1011, which classified every prompt-sending module in the suite. See #1010.

THE FOUR, with what each embeds and who authors it:

1. packages/spec-lint/lib/llm.mjs:14-16,31 — `${items}`, built from `verifiedCriteria.map((c,i) => `${i}: ${c.text}`)`. Acceptance-criterion text, authored by whoever filed the work.
2. packages/lesson-foundry/lib/llm.mjs:20-22 — `${clusterName}` and `${JSON.stringify(samples, null, 2)}`. Prosecution findings — model-authored text being fed back into a model.
3. packages/premortem/lib/prompt.mjs:11 — `buildPrompt(specContent)` returns `specContent.trim() + instructions`. The ENTIRE spec file, unfenced, and placed BEFORE the instructions.
4. packages/consensus-fix/lib/prompt.mjs:31,40 — `tailedOutput` (raw output of a failing test run) and per-file `excerpt.text`, each wrapped in markdown triple backticks only. A triple backtick is escaped by writing a triple backtick, which test output can trivially contain.

WHAT TO BUILD

Route each embedded value through `fence(label, content, maxChars)` from @adlc/core. All four packages already declare @adlc/core as a dependency, so no package.json change is needed; premortem/lib/prompt.mjs currently imports nothing and needs the import added. Match each file's existing import style (the other three use `from '@adlc/core'`).

Caps — state the chosen cap as a named module-level constant in each file, do not inline a magic number:
  - spec-lint: the joined criteria block. 8000, matching the TICKET_TEXT_MAX_CHARS convention used elsewhere.
  - lesson-foundry: fence the cluster name and the samples JSON SEPARATELY, so a hostile cluster name cannot break out through the JSON block. 8000 for the samples, 200 for the name.
  - consensus-fix: testOutput is already tail()'d to 4000 — fence at that same 4000 so the cap is not applied twice. Fence each file excerpt individually, replacing its ``` block; 8000 each.
  - premortem: SPECIAL CASE, read carefully. The spec IS the payload, so any cap truncates the artifact under review, and fence() tail-biases, which would silently drop the spec's OPENING sections (that is #1007). Use a deliberately generous cap (64000) and add a comment naming #1007 and explaining why the number is large rather than the 8000 used elsewhere. Do NOT reorder the prompt so the spec comes last as a workaround — the instruction text must remain clearly outside the fence, which fencing already achieves.

Also move all four files from UNGUARDED_REVIEWED into GUARDED in scripts/test/prompt-fencing.test.mjs, each with mustContain naming its fence() call and mustNotMatch naming the raw interpolation it replaces. The sweep must stay green with zero UNGUARDED_REVIEWED entries for these four — an entry left behind pointing at #1010 after the fix is a stale allowlist entry and the sweep's own staleness test will catch it.

WRITE THE RED TESTS FIRST. For each builder, a test that feeds a hostile payload containing a forged closing marker and asserts (a) the payload appears inside the fence, and (b) the fence's real terminator is not the forged one. Each must fail before the change. Three existing test files assert prompt shape and will need updating: packages/spec-lint/test/spec-lint.test.mjs, packages/premortem/test/premortem.test.mjs, packages/consensus-fix/test/prompt.test.mjs.

DO NOT modify packages/core/lib/text.mjs. It is a declared rail on this ticket: this work consumes the fence primitive, it does not change it. If fence() seems to need a change, stop and say so rather than editing it.

OUT OF SCOPE: tail()'s truncation direction (#1007) and the mutation-gate zero-mutant gap (#1013).

ACCEPTANCE
- Each of the four builders routes its externally-authored content through fence(); a hostile fixture with a forged terminator cannot close any of them. Verified by a per-package test that fails before the change.
- scripts/test/prompt-fencing.test.mjs lists all four in GUARDED and none in UNGUARDED_REVIEWED, and the sweep still passes.
- The sweep still goes red on a planted prompt-sender in a sibling package (probe NOT in packages/core/lib — a file there imports './llm.mjs' relatively and the from-core detector cannot see it).
- `npm test` green from the repo root, output shown.
- `adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this ticket id>` exits 0, proving packages/core/lib/text.mjs was not touched.
title: Fence the four prompt builders that embed externally-authored content raw (#1010)
